key: local perception on environmental impact of coal mining in odisha india
title: Local Perception on Environmental Impact of Coal Mining in  Odisha, India
venue: South Asian Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
abstract: Coal mining contributes significantly to a nation's growth and development but also threatens the environment and health. This research examines local perceptions of coal mining's impact in Odisha. A household survey was conducted in five villages surrounding the Bhubaneswari,  Bharatpur and Lingaraj coal mining regions. The research draws on the local community's  views on environmental degradation due to coal mining. Findings revealed that 82 per cent of  respondents reported changes in forest cover, 78 per cent believed air and water quality had  deteriorated, and 59 per cent reported wildlife and biodiversity loss. Water issues in the  mining area are a serious concern. 78 per cent reported poor water quality. This study used a  logistic regression model to analyse the relationship between air quality status and forest  resource loss, biodiversity loss, fuel use and dust pollution. Biodiversity loss is a significant  predictor. Although Mahanadi Coalfield Limited has adopted measures under CSR and  sustainable development initiatives, only a minority of households report satisfaction with  their effectiveness. The results highlight the paradox of coal mining in Odisha: economic  benefits are widespread, but environmental externalities burden local communities, reflecting  elements of the resource curse hypothesis. The study underscores the need for stronger  institutional frameworks, transparent governance, and coordinated policies among local  communities, the state government, and coal mining companies to mitigate long-term  ecological problems. This research work contributed to the broader theoretical discourse on  natural resource governance by linking the findings to the resource curse hypothesis.

key: overtourism and environmental disasters in bali indonesia can it be approached through emp
title: Overtourism and Environmental Disasters in Bali, Indonesia: Can it be approached through empowerment?
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
abstract: The pressure to achieve sustainable tourism has become a top priority for tourist destinations worldwide, and Bali, Indonesia, is one of the best examples of a place suffering from overtourism. Tourist arrivals have increased from 4,001,835 in 2015 to 6,275,210 in 2019, which has made the island face serious environmental issues such as the demand for clean water accounting for about 65 percent of the total supply. This paper explores how community empowerment can play a role in solving the environmental problems resulting from overtourism in Bali. The research design was a qualitative case study in Cemenggaon Traditional Village, Gianyar, with 10 informants chosen through purposive sampling, in-depth interviews, field observations, and document analysis were the data collection methods, and Miles and Huberman’s interactive model was the data analysis method. The results show that community empowerment via the PESAN-PEDE Program, the teba modern system of composting, a community waste bank, and customary regulations (perarem) have been instrumental in enhancing the capacity of the community in facing environmental pressures, while residents have been engaged as the main actors, instead of being passive recipients of government policies. This means that community empowerment, along with being a tool for environmental management, is a locally grounded and sustainable development strategy that can be a reference for other overtourism-affected destinations in Bali and beyond.

key: assessing the impacts of flooding on environmental sustainability and livelihoods in tonj
title: Assessing the Impacts of Flooding on Environmental Sustainability and Livelihoods in Tonj Payam, Warrap State, South Sudan
venue: African Journal of Climate and Resilience
abstract: Flooding is a major environmental hazard in South Sudan, but its impact on livelihoods in Tonj Payam, Warrap State, remains undocumented. This study assessed the causes and impacts of flooding, community coping mechanisms, and the groups most affected. The mixed-methods design combined a questionnaire with key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Cochran’s formula yielded a sample of 280 respondents, comprising officials, traditional authorities, and household heads across Tonj Payam. Most respondents were male (60.7%), married (91.4%), and without formal education (77.5%); small-scale farming was the dominant livelihood (65.4%). Overflow of the Tonj River (91.8%) and an unpaved road (87.9%) were the leading causes of flooding, which caused widespread loss of life and property, disrupted trade, and degraded soil and vegetation. Elderly people, children, and women were disproportionately affected. The study recommends relocating vulnerable households to higher ground, building drainage canals, and enforcing zoning to protect wetlands and drainage channels.

key: the dynamics and implications of landuse and landcover change in bayelsa state
title: The Dynamics and Implications of Landuse and Landcover Change in Bayelsa State
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Social Sciences, Environmental Studies & Technology
abstract: This study examines the dynamics and implications of landuse and landcover change in Sagbama LGA of Bayelsa State. Satellite imageries of 1987, 1992, and 2015 were derived from the USGS, Using supervised classification, bare land surfaces reduced significantly from 46km2 in 1987 to 40km2 in the year 1992 and 11km2 in 2015. The built-up areas/developed areas increased from 10km2 in the year 1987 to 46km2 in 1992 and 61km2 in 2015. Area covered by light vegetation increased from 316km2 in 1987 to 404km2 in 1992 and 511km2 in 2015, while heavy vegetation reduced from 526km2 in 1987 to 408km2 in 1992 and 315km2 in 2015. The logistic regression results showed that education, gender, agricultural land use, and logging of trees are (1.0, 1.1, 1.2, and 1.6) times more likely to influence land cover change at a 0.05 significance level. This study recommends government implementation of the policy of controlled logging and the involvement of non-governmental agencies in public enlightenment to protect the environment, and improve the livelihood of residents in the coastal communities ofBayelsa State.

key: sustainable strategies for the urbanization of agricultural and forest lands
title: SUSTAINABLE STRATEGIES FOR THE URBANIZATION OF AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST LANDS
venue: Proceedings of International Structural Engineering and Construction
abstract: Human activities that degrade the natural environment have intensified sustainability challenges, particularly in rapidly urbanizing regions. In Gaziantep, one of the most densely populated cities in Southeastern Anatolia, recent urban expansion has converted agricultural and forest lands into residential areas, creating risks for environmental, social, and economic sustainability. This study specifically investigates the İbrahimli and Erikçe districts, formerly agricultural and forest areas now inhabited largely by upper-income families, to examine how urban development affects sustainability. The research applies a novel combination of field photography, SWOT analysis, and expert surveys to develop and evaluate strategic scenarios aimed at mitigating further environmental and social impacts. Data were analyzed using SPSS, and the results indicate that establishing a social center is the most suitable strategy for İbrahimli, whereas halting development or converting the area into recreational space is most appropriate for Erikçe. The study provides actionable insights for managing urban growth while balancing multiple sustainability objectives.

key: distribution of ukrainian farms by size and sustainability in agriculture
title: Distribution of Ukrainian Farms by Size and Sustainability in Agriculture
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
abstract: The study presented in this article examines the distribution of Ukrainian agricultural enterprises by their size and concentration of land resources broken down by statistical groups of enterprises. Based on official data for the period from 2020 to 2025, the Gini coefficient was calculated at 0,732 – 0,763, Lorenz curves were plotted, and it was concluded that there is a significant risk of monopolisation of control over land. A factor analysis was carried out depending on the area of agricultural land under control and number of enterprises. Changes were displayed using an index method similar to the decomposition approach, and the logarithmic dynamic of relative changes was assessed and identified, the farms were losing their share of control at the fastest rate, while the group of the largest ones saw an increase in the average area per enterprise, indicating further consolidation. Using these calculation results, as well as the findings regarding the increase in the use of fertilisers and pesticides, the article analyses the potential risks to the sustainable development of Ukraine’s agricultural sector associated with the consolidation of land parcels, combined with a reduction in the number of smallholdings and the threat of monopolisation.

key: evaluation of petroleum hydrocarbon pollution in soil environment impacted by illegal arti
title: Evaluation of Petroleum Hydrocarbon Pollution in Soil Environment Impacted by Illegal Artisanal Refining in Bayelsa, Nigeria
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHEMISTRY AND CHEMICAL PROCESSES
abstract:
Illegal artisanal refining of crude oil is widespread in the Niger Delta and poses serious threats
to soil quality, ecosystem function and human health. This study evaluated the extent, composition,
and potential impacts of petroleum hydrocarbon pollution in soils impacted by illegal artisanal
refining of crud in from Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Soil samples were collected from two major
artisanal refining hotspots and from a background (unimpacted) location. Total petroleum
hydrocarbons (TPH) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were analyzed GC-MS
following standard procedures. Speciation of the PAH compound was also carried out. Results
indicated markedly elevated concentrations of TPH and PAHs in soils at refining sites relative to
background areas, with distinct spatial hotspots proximal to where refining operations lasted
longer. PAH profiles showed predominance of higher-molecular-weight, persistent compounds,
including those with known carcinogenicity. Risk calculations signaled both ecological and
human-health concerns. The findings point to the need for targeted remediation, continuous
environmental monitoring, stronger enforcement of regulations and community-centered
alternatives to artisanal refining. The study provides a baseline for remediation planning and for
policymaking to reduce long-term environmental and public-health burdens in Bayelsa.

key: evidence based random forestgoogle earth engine protocol for rainfed paddy monitoring in a
title: Evidence-Based Random Forest–Google Earth Engine Protocol for Rainfed Paddy Monitoring in Aceh
abstract:
Background: Rainfed paddy fields are the most climate-vulnerable segment of food-crop land, yet they are the least adequately represented in spatial databases. On the east coast of Aceh, Indonesia, North Aceh Regency holds 8,356 ha of rainfed paddy distributed across 27 sub-districts, equivalent to 21.02% of its 39,762 ha of cultivated baseline paddy land, while Bireuen Regency holds 2,784.91 ha across 13 sub-districts, equivalent to 18.64% of its 14,944 ha. Taken together, 11,140.91 ha, or 20.37% of the paddy land in both regencies, depends entirely on rainfall. Between 2021 and 2023 the harvested rice area contracted by 29.07% in North Aceh and by 10.14% in Bireuen, while yields in North Aceh declined from 5.77 to 5.38 t ha⁻¹. 
Objective: Optical monitoring in this region is constrained by cloud cover that peaks in October and November, precisely the land-preparation and transplanting window of rainfed fields. 
Methods: This study adopts a systematic evidence-synthesis design covering 13 published land cover classification and rice mapping studies, combined with an analysis of official secondary statistics, in order to quantify the scale of the rainfed paddy problem on the east coast of Aceh, to benchmark the performance of the Random Forest algorithm on the Google Earth Engine platform using published empirical evidence, and to formulate a cloud-resilient operational monitoring protocol. 
Results: The synthesis shows that optical-based Random Forest achieves a mean overall accuracy of 94.34% (range 89.00–98.81%; standard deviation 3.52) with a mean Kappa coefficient of 0.8926, and consistently outperforms CART by 4.87 percentage points of overall accuracy and by 0.107 Kappa points. Optical–radar fusion schemes attain comparable accuracy (mean 94.65%) without depending on the availability of cloud-free imagery, and the evidence indicates that preserving the temporal dimension of the image time series raises accuracy by up to 14.7% for Sentinel-1 data. 
Conclusion: On this basis, a ten-class monitoring protocol comprising 104 predictor variables, a four-layer cloud-handling chain, and explicit rules for separating rainfed from irrigated paddy is proposed, accompanied by a ready-to-run Google Earth Engine script provided as an appendix.

key: depopulation and land use changes in serbia challenges and perspectives in the 21st centur
title: Depopulation and land use changes in Serbia: Challenges and perspectives in the 21st century
venue: Population and Environment: Challenges and Perspectives - Book of abstracts - zbornik radova
abstract: Since the late 20th century, Serbia has experienced a continuous population decline. Census data from 1991 already indicate a negative demographic trend in all regions of Serbia, except for the Belgrade region (excluding Kosovo and Metohija). Certain municipalities deviate from this trend due to a positive natural population increase (Novi Pazar, Sjenica, Tutin) or a positive migration balance (Novi Sad, Belgrade). However, these cases represent exceptions rather than the dominant demographic processes in the country. Research has shown that depopulation has direct environmental implications, including changes in soil erosion intensity, the frequency of flash floods, and pollution levels. Several studies in Serbia have analyzed the impact of demographic changes on land use and land cover (LULC) transformations, particularly in urban areas (Belgrade, Novi Sad - Futog), forest ecosystems (South Banat District), agricultural land and erosion-prone areas (the Velika Morava and South Morava river basins), and in abandoned rural settlements in western, southern, and Eastern Serbia. Additionally, studies have examined LULC changes at the national level without directly considering the effects of depopulation. Findings indicate a correlation between demographic decline and LULC changes. However, besides depopulation, various socio-economic factors also influence these transformations and should be considered in further analyses. Notably, Vojvodina, Serbia's traditional agricultural region, remains underrepresented in existing research, despite the potential significance of studying LULC changes in this area. Understanding LULC dynamics and their relationship with demographic processes is a crucial step toward effective spatial planning and sustainable development.

key: tracing the invisible footprint of mining in iran spectral mapping of heavy metal contamin
title: Tracing the invisible footprint of mining in Iran: spectral mapping of heavy metal contamination in arid soils with a remote sensing approach
abstract: This research applies an interdisciplinary framework to investigate the interactions between mining activities, heavy metal contamination, and vegetation response in the Sangan mining areas of Khaf County, Iran. Geochemical analyses of 24 surface soil samples were integrated with remote sensing data from Landsat 8-OLI to develop a robust methodology for monitoring stressed ecosystems. Chemical analysis revealed substantial accumulation of cadmium (Cd, barium (Ba) and arsenic (As). The mean Cd concentration (26.5 mg kg⁻¹) was about 88 times higher than the global shale average (0.3 mg kg⁻¹), which is likely associated with to intensive iron ore mining. This finding underscores the risk of these metals entering the food chain and threatening human health, especially in children, who exhibit higher absorption rates. From a remote-sensing perspective, soil-adjusted vegetation indices such as RVI (R = 0.82) and MSAVI2 (R = 0.79) outperformed NDVI (R = 0.40) in arid environments with sparse vegetation, providing a methodological advance for ecological monitoring. Correlation analyses between heavy metals and vegetation indices revealed a strong negative association between copper (Cu) and most indices, particularly IPVI (R = − 0.69), indicating copper’s phytotoxic effects on chlorophyll and biomass. In contrast, chromium (Cr) showed a weak positive correlation with NDVI (R = 0.36). These results highlight the need to select vegetation indices according to local environmental conditions and offer a practical framework for enhancing remote sensing–based monitoring of contaminated ecosystems. The study improves understanding of mining impacts and provides a replicable model for sustainable management of mining-affected landscapes worldwide.

key: analyzing technosphere fire consequences in irkutsk region
title: Analyzing technosphere fire consequences in Irkutsk region
abstract: Using the case of Irkutsk region, the problem of the consequences of man-made and natural fires is examined based on their main indicators (number of fires, number of dead and injured people, destroyed facilities, as well as direct material damage) for 2019–2024. The factual basis for the study was fire statistics in residential, public, industrial, and other technosphere facilities. It was found that during this period, the region experienced an average of up to 6,000 fires annually, with damage exceeding 480 million rubles (five percent of the regional budget). More than 180 people died in the fires, and about 200 were injured. Over 1,500 facilities of various functional purposes were destroyed. It was demonstrated that the fire situation in Irkutsk region is one of the important factors affecting the living conditions of the population. At the same time, each fire constitutes social and economic damage, resulting not only in financial and property losses but also in human casualties. Based on a set of statistical indicators for the observed years, an analysis of the fire hazard situation was carried out across the region, its urban agglomerations, and rural areas. Considerable attention is paid to the analysis of annual indicators of fire consequences, taking into account such quantitative changes as absolute growth, the growth rate, and the rate of increase. New forms of preventive work with the population are proposed.

key: the role of domestic and international markets in the loss of nature across brazil
title: The role of domestic and international markets in the loss of nature across Brazil
abstract: Humans have converted a vast area of nature—forests, savannahs, wetlands, and grasslands—for agriculture. Though domestic markets account for more than 70% of global agricultural production and land use change, domestic supply chains and end-uses are rarely mapped. Here, we present an inter-regional input–output model for Brazil, a major agricultural producer and market with an active agricultural frontier, experiencing 70 Mha hectares of vegetation conversion since 2000. We capture the drivers of conversion in each of Brazil’s six biomes from 2010–2015, linking them to 36 economic sectors and 47 Brazilian regions and four external trading partners: the European Union, the United States, China, and the Rest of the World. We find that 37.8% of conversion was driven by local (within-state) consumption, 35.2% driven by demand from other Brazilian states, and the remaining 27% for international trade. Overall, the area of non-forest conversion exceeded that of forests, notably for the domestic market and exports to China. Our approach reveals how conversion percolates throughout the economy, with many sectors indirectly sourcing conversion-associated products and by-products. Notably, we link 10.3% of conversion to dairy consumption and 7.9% of conversion to service sectors, such as Horeca (hotels, restaurants, and cafés). While current environmental governance efforts largely focus on zero-deforestation pledges and first-mile traceability (e.g. from farms to slaughterhouses) our results provide a basis for accountability efforts to look upstream, engaging the retail, dairy, leather, and processed food sectors which use products linked to the loss of nature across each of Brazil’s biomes.

key: economic value of coral reefs the case study of mu ko chang national park trat province th
title: Economic Value of Coral Reefs: The Case Study of Mu Ko Chang National Park, Trat Province, Thailand
venue: Journal of Applied Economics and Management Strategy
abstract: The past decade has witnessed a substantial rise in ecotourism, providing a major economic boost to many developing countries, including Thailand's second-largest island, Ko Chang in Trat Province. Protected areas like Mu Ko Chang National Park face critical challenges in reconciling economic development with conservation. This paper contributes to understanding the role of economic analysis in protected area management by estimating the recreational benefit (consumer surplus) of the coral reefs in Mu Ko Chang, Trat province, using the Individual Travel Cost Method (ITCM). Data were collected via direct interviews with 592 visitors. The results indicate that the recreational services of the park generate an estimated annual consumer surplus of 2,025.92 million Baht (USD 61.73 million), of which international visitors account for the largest share (1,298.13 million Baht). The present recreational value over 30 years is calculated to be 25,139.48 million Baht (USD 794.75 million) (using a 7% discount rate). Crucially, demand analysis revealed distinct market behaviors: Domestic demand aligns with a normal good and is inelastic to price, while international demand is negatively income elastic (indicating substitution as wealth rises) but strongly and positively driven by educational attainment. The findings demonstrate the substantial economic importance of coral reef ecosystems and support the implementation of a tiered entrance fee system and conservation funding mechanisms to enhance sustainable tourism management and long-term marine ecosystem conservation.

key: global potash industry in 20052025 resource base mining and market constraints
title: Global potash industry in 2005–2025: resource base, mining and market constraints
abstract: The paper clarifies current development trends in the global potash industry with regard to the resource base, production structure, pricing environment and investment constraints in 2005–2025. Unlike studies that are focused mainly on the agrochemical market, this article treats potash salts as an object of the mining industry planning, where the geography of reserves, mine commissioning schedules, logistical resilience, and market and environmental constraints are of key importance. Methodologically, the study is based on comparing statistics from the U.S. Geological Survey, analytical materials from the FAO, the IFA and the World Bank, industry publications and data on major capacity-expansion projects. The results show that the global market remains highly concentrated, i.e. Canada, Russia, Belarus, China and Germany account for the main share of production, while the resource base is distributed much wider than the current operating capacity. In 2025, world potash production reached 49 million tonnes of K2O, the consumption was estimated at 38.8 million tonnes of K2O, and the aggregate capacity is projected to increase from 66.1 million tonnes of K2O in 2025 to 77.4 million tonnes of K2O by 2029. The industry’s development will be determined not only by the growing food demand, but also by the companies’ ability to overcome capital intensity challenges, environmental requirements and geopolitical constraints on supply [1–4].

key: impact of anthropogenic activities agriculture mining urbanization on vegetation and soils
title: IMPACT OF ANTHROPOGENIC ACTIVITIES (AGRICULTURE, MINING, URBANIZATION) ON VEGETATION AND SOILS IN MARITIME GUINEA (2002–2024)
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
abstract: The sub-prefecture of Damakhania, in Maritime Guinea, is undergoing rapid landscape transformation driven by the The landscapes of the Damakhania sub-prefecture, in Maritime Guinea, are being rapidly reshaped by the combined effects of urban expansion, agriculture and climate variability. This study examines changes in vegetation and hydroclimatic conditions between 1986 and 2024, quantifies land-use/land-cover (LULC) change between 2002 and 2024, and explores possible trajectories up to 2100. Fifteen variables were analysed: seven Landsat-derived indices (NDVI, EVI, SAVI, MSAVI, NBR, NDWI and LST) and eight climatic and water-balance variables. Trends and change points were assessed with the Mann-Kendall, Sen's slope and Pettitt tests, and seasonal contrasts with Student's t-test and the Mann-Whitney test. LULC maps for 2002 (Landsat 5 TM) and 2024 (Landsat 8 OLI) were used to measure change and to build three prospective scenarios. EVI declined significantly (τ = −0.385; p < 0.001), whereas land surface temperature rose by about 0.23 °C per year (τ = 0.397; p < 0.001). The Pettitt test indicated significant inhomogeneity in the EVI, NBR and LST series, while precipitation, maximum air temperature and NDVI showed no significant trend. Over 22 years, wooded/shrub savanna and open forest lost 47.4% and 45.7% of their area, respectively, to the benefit of urban fabric (+203.4%), degraded areas and bare soil (+189.7%) and crops and fallow land (+33.5%). The scenarios suggest that, without conservation measures, natural vegetation could disappear before 2050. The observed degradation appears more closely related to human pressure than to an unfavourable rainfall trend, which calls for land-use planning that protects the remaining wooded areas.

key: urban streams in petrolina pernambuco environmental degradation and challenges for water m
title: URBAN STREAMS IN PETROLINA, PERNAMBUCO: ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION AND CHALLENGES FOR WATER MANAGEMENT

key: environmental effects of artisanal mining on the livelihood of rural settlements in endo c
title: Environmental Effects of Artisanal Mining on the Livelihood of Rural Settlements in Endo Community, Nasarawa Local Government Area, Nasarawa State, Nigeria
venue: Azman University International Journal of Management and Social Sciences
abstract: Artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) has become a prevalent non-farm rural livelihood practice among mineral-bearing communities in Nasarawa State, but its environmental impact on host communities is poorly understood. This study analyses the environmental effects of ASM on the livelihoods of rural communities in Endo, a community located within Nasarawa Local Government Area of Nasarawa State, Nigeria. Based on the Sustainable Livelihood Approach, the study adopted a descriptive survey design in which data were collected from 150 respondents comprising artisanal miners, farmers, and household heads, supplemented with key informant interviews and field observations. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics (frequencies, percentages, and mean scores) and Pearson Product Moment Correlation analysis. The findings revealed that ASM has resulted in land degradation, deforestation, water pollution, soil erosion, and loss of farmland, while also providing income diversification and employment opportunities for community members. The study further established a statistically significant relationship between the intensity of ASM activities and the decline of traditional rural livelihood practices such as crop production and fishing. The study recommends stricter enforcement of the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act, community-based environmental monitoring, mine-site reclamation, and livelihood diversification programmes for affected households.

key: implementation of a wastewater treatment plant wwtp in the patarcocha lagoon for complianc
title: Implementation of a Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) in the Patarcocha Lagoon for Compliance with Environmental Law, Pasco – 2025
venue: European Journal of Prosthodontics and Restorative Dentistry
abstract:
This research was conducted in the district of Chaupimarca, province and
region of Pasco, an area directly affected by the pollution of Patarcocha
Lagoon. The study contributes to technical and legal decision-making aimed
at reducing the negative impacts of untreated domestic wastewater discharge,
seepage, and rainwater runoff during the rainy season. Located in the urban
center of the city of Cerro de Pasco, this lagoon is a natural body of water of
high ecological and social importance; its deterioration directly affects the
population's quality of life, public health, and local ecosystem.
Geographically, the lagoon sits at an altitude of approximately 4,360 meters
above sea level, with a surface area of 34,800 square meters, a perimeter of
1,400 meters, and an average depth of 14 meters. This site represents a
critical point for compliance with environmental law. Since the 1970s,
pollution has continuously increased, worsening drastically in the 1990s due
to the influx of untreated wastewater from 120 surrounding homes. These
dwellings—along with the Túpac Amaru, Víctor Arias Vicuña, and
Tahuantinsuyo informal settlements, as well as Moquegua, Bolognesi,
Alfonso Ugarte, Yauli streets, and the Túpac Amaru ring road—constitute
the main sources of direct domestic discharge. In response, a series of
recovery strategies are proposed: implementing a Wastewater Treatment
Plant (WWTP) at the outlet of the collector ring's discharge, followed by an
ecological restoration project for Patarcocha Lagoon carried out in
collaboration with local residents and supported by the Provincial Municipal
Government of Pasco and the Regional Government of Pasco.

key: analisis espacial de la dinamica del paisaje forestal en mesoamerica 2015 2022
title: Análisis espacial de la dinámica del paisaje forestal en Mesoamérica (2015-2022)
authors: G. De la Fuente de Val
abstract: The transformation of the Mesoamerican landscape is degrading broadleaf and montane forests, increasing their vulnerability and ecosystem risk. The research analyzed the relationship between transformation, fragmentation, and anthropogenic threats in Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, and Honduras, with the aim of generating spatial evidence to prioritize areas for ecological restoration. Forest cover data from 2015 and 2022, landscape metrics, and Markovian land-use change models were used, integrated with criteria A2a, B1, and B2 of the Red List of Ecosystems. The results show losses of undisturbed forest of 55.3% in Mexico and 35.2% in Guatemala. In Honduras, fragmentation increased by 99.7%, while in El Salvador deforested land could increase by 872% by 2030. These trends are associated with agricultural and livestock expansion, urbanization, and forest fires. It is concluded that ecosystem risk arises from the spatial interaction between cover loss, fragmentation, and human pressures. The integration of spatial analysis, change modeling, and risk assessment offers a useful tool for guiding ecological restoration, strengthening territorial planning, and targeting interventions in the most vulnerable forest landscapes of Mesoamerica over the coming decades through sustainable strategic decisions.

key: impact assessment of okobo coal mine in kogi state nigeria using the rapid impact assessme
title: Impact Assessment of Okobo Coal Mine in Kogi State, Nigeria, Using the Rapid Impact Assessment Matrix (RIAM)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive assessment of the geo-environmental and socio-economic impacts of coal mining and deposits in the Okobo district of Ankpa Local Government Area, Kogi State, Nigeria. The research quantitatively evaluates heavy metal contamination and the presence of Acid Mine Drainage (AMD) resulting from both historical and persistent illegal mining activities. Using a quantitative approach, soil and water samples were analyzed, and the Rapid Impact Assessment Matrix (RIAM) was applied to evaluate the significance of various impacts on key environmental and social components. The findings revealed widespread heavy metal contamination, with elevated concentrations of Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, Pb, Cd, and Ni in soil and water samples, often exceeding permissible environmental limits. For instance, Mn concentrations in water ranged from 0.44 to 0.81 mg/L, surpassing the 0.2 mg/L WHO standard. The pH of water samples varied from 3.2 to 6.9, with strong acidity in some locations confirming the presence of AMD. The RIAM analysis underscored high negative impacts across various environmental and socio-economic components, corroborating the observed contamination. The study concludes that coal mining in the Okobo district has severely compromised the region’s environmental integrity, presenting a critical environmental and public health concern. Based on these findings, urgent remediation strategies, stringent enforcement against illegal mining, and continuous environmental monitoring are recommended to mitigate the adverse effects and promote sustainable post-mining land-use plans. This research provides a crucial baseline for future environmental policy and intervention in coal-mining affected regions of Nigeria.

key: evaluasi daya dukung das jompi berdasarkan permenhut p 61 menhut ii 2014 di pulau muna ind
title: Evaluasi Daya Dukung DAS Jompi berdasarkan Permenhut P.61/MENHUT-II/2014 di Pulau Muna, Indonesia
venue: Jurnal ilmiah membangun desa dan pertanian
abstract: The Jompi Watershed on Muna Island is under increasing environmental pressure from land-use change and human activities, threatening its carrying capacity. This study assessed watershed management performance using the integrated carrying capacity framework of the Indonesian Minister of Forestry Regulation No. P.61/Menhut-II/2014. Conducted from June to November 2023 in the 5,141.62 ha Jompi Watershed, the assessment applied a weighted scoring method covering land condition, water management, socio-economic and institutional aspects, water infrastructure investment, and spatial land use. The results showed that 30.23% of the watershed was classified as critical land, with an erosion index of 11.53, indicating severe degradation despite 95.69% vegetation cover. Hydrological indicators included a Flow Regime Coefficient of 7.27, an Annual Runoff Coefficient of 0.25, sediment yield of 26.42 t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹, annual flooding, and a Water Use Index of 3,023.26. Population pressure on land was low (0.26), but 29.72% of households were categorized as poor. The overall carrying capacity score was 108.25, placing the watershed in the moderate category. Critical land, erosion, sedimentation, and low community welfare were identified as the main limiting factors. Land rehabilitation, erosion control, and improved water resource management are recommended to ensure long-term watershed sustainability.

key: socio economic characteristics and livelihoods in abujas informal enclaves the case of kpa
title: Socio-Economic Characteristics and Livelihoods in Abuja’s Informal Enclaves: The Case of Kpaduma
venue: Journal of Innovative Social Science and Humanities Research
abstract: The expansion of informal settlements remains a primary structural challenge for cities across the Global South, a reality clearly visible in rapidly growing administrative capitals like Abuja (UN-Habitat, 2022; United Nations, 2023). This study investigates the socio-economic profiles, housing conditions, and survival strategies of households living in Kpaduma, an unplanned enclave sitting directly along the boundary of the affluent Guzape District (Cadastral Zone A09). Primary data were gathered through 384 household surveys, informant interviews with municipal officials, and structured field observations, paired with an analysis of Federal Capital Territory (FCT) planning documents. The findings show that Kpaduma operates as a critical, low-cost housing hub for the city’s low-wage workforce, including junior civil servants, artisans, and informal traders. However, basic infrastructure is almost entirely absent: nearly 80% of households rely on informal water vendors or unsafe wells, while rudimentary drainage and poor waste handling, create persistent environmental health risks. Pervasive tenure insecurity further exposes residents to eviction threats and deters long-term investment in home improvements. Ultimately, despite being economically integrated into Abuja's labor market, Kpaduma remains institutionally excluded. The study argues that aggressive clearance policies fail to resolve urban growth challenges, advocating instead for in-situ upgrading, land tenure regularization, and inclusive zoning within FCT planning frameworks.

key: hydro chemical trend of tlawng and tuirial rivers in aizawl district india a review of lit
title: HYDRO-CHEMICAL TREND OF TLAWNG AND TUIRIAL RIVERS IN AIZAWL DISTRICT, INDIA: A REVIEW OF LITERATURE (2023–2026)
abstract: Water security is a very critical issue in Mizoram, with most of the mountainous areas relying heavily on available bigger surface water sources, such as rivers Tlawng and Tuirial that are influenced by the monsoons. These water bodies are very important for drinking, agricultural and domestic purposes in Aizawl district but are constantly being degraded. In this review paper, we have discussed the hydro-chemical characteristics and found that both the rivers were under significant stress due to seasonal changes and unmanaged anthropogenic activities. The quality of raw water was significantly degraded by anthropogenic influences such as untreated municipal sewage, medical waste, agricultural runoff and dumping along river banks. Turbidity, acidity and organic loads were high during monsoons due to hydro-climatic cycles, while dry low flows led to accumulation of dissolved solids, hardness and alkalinity. Alarming levels of coliform contamination were found in raw Tlawng water. Moreover, there is a critical gap in the published literature due to the absence of empirical monitoring of the Tuirial River since 2021. These problems can be addressed by upgrading municipal treatment plants, regulating healthcare effluents and promoting continuous research and publications for targeted river basins.

key: towards establishing coastal greenbelts for disaster risk reduction and mitigation
title: Towards Establishing Coastal Greenbelts for Disaster Risk Reduction and Mitigation
abstract:
Mangrove ecosystems provide essential goods and services, with storm protection being their most valuable contribution at an estimated US$8,966‒10,821 per hectare. In the Philippines, the need for this coastal defense is urgent due to intense storms, such as the 2013 super Typhoon Haiyan, which have caused thousands of fatalities and billions of dollars in infrastructure and agricultural damage. Unfortunately, historical mangrove cover in the country drastically declined from approximately 450,000 hectares to just 120,000 hectares by 1994–1995, largely due to the conversion of these areas into aquaculture ponds.
Scientific reviews demonstrate that establishing a 100-meter-wide vegetation buffer can effectively reduce wind and swell wave heights by 13% to 60%. While national mandates like the Coastal Greenbelt Bill remain pending in Congress, local government units and national agencies are leading the charge to legislate and establish these protective coastal greenbelts.
Successful greenbelt establishment requires comprehensive and varied strategies, including the integration of beach forests in areas where mangroves cannot naturally grow. A critical component of this effort is reverting abandoned fishponds back to mangroves—as demonstrated by the Leganes Integrated Katunggan Ecopark—which is necessary to achieve an ecologically sustainable 4:1 mangrove-to-pond ratio. Furthermore, for severely eroded coastlines, Green-Gray Engineering interventions like rock-mound breakwaters are essential to restore the substrate elevation required for healthy mangrove growth.

key: export potential and decarbonization of the russian mining and metallurgical complex amid
title: Export potential and decarbonization of the Russian mining and metallurgical complex amid the transformation of the world economy
abstract: The study examines the export potential and decarbonization path of the Russian mining and metallurgical complex amid the transformation of the world economy and emergence of the carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM). Its relevance is defined by the deepening crisis of the core subsectors in 2023–2025: with coal production stabilizing at about 440 million tonnes, exports recovered to 211 million tonnes by the end of 2025 (+7.5% compared to 2024), yet the net financial result of the coal industry went down from a profit of RUB 374.7 billion in 2023 to losses of RUB 112.6 billion in 2024 and RUB 408 billion in 2025 (a 3.6-fold increase in losses), while the share of profitable companies fell from 68.5% to 33.9%. Crude steel output declined from 76.0 million tonnes in 2023 to 67.8 million tonnes in 2025 (a seven-year low) against the world production of 1,849 million tonnes (−2%). The hypothesis is that the competitiveness of the Russian mining and metallurgical complex is determined not by the volume of physical supplies, but by the capacity to reduce the specific carbon intensity of products and to diversify sales markets. The objective is to justify directions for adapting the export-oriented Russian mining and metallurgical complex to decarbonization of the world economy on the basis of production, export, financial, and emission indicators. The methods applied include comparative subsector analysis, industry benchmarking of the carbon intensity, and indicator analysis of the emission load. It was established that the carbon intensity of blast-furnace–and- oxygen converter steelmaking (2.30 t of CO2-eq./t) exceeds the world average (1.85) by 24% and it is 1.53 times higher than the direct reduction using the electric-arc furnace method (1.50); with the CBAM certificate price of EUR 75.36/t of CO2 (Q1 2026) and full coverage of the emissions (by 2034) the direct carbon load will reach EUR 139–173 per tonne of steel; ferrous and non-ferrous metallurgy together generate 28% of the Russian greenhouse gas emissions. Three adaptation directions are justified, i.e. diversification of markets and logistics, technological reduction of the carbon intensity, and alignment of the national carbon units system with the export agenda.

key: evaluation of petroleum hydrocarbon pollution in soils impacted by artisanal refining in b
title: Evaluation of Petroleum Hydrocarbon Pollution in Soils Impacted by Artisanal Refining in Bayelsa, Nigeria
venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF CHEMISTRY AND CHEMICAL PROCESSES
abstract:
Artisanal refining of crude oil is widespread in the Niger Delta and poses serious threats to soil
quality, ecosystem function and human health. This study evaluated the extent, composition and
potential impacts of petroleum hydrocarbon pollution in soils impacted by artisanal refining of
crude oil in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. Soil samples were collected from two major artisanal refining
hotspots and from a background location. Total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) and polycyclic
aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were analyzed using GC-MS, following standard procedures.
Speciation of the PAHs was also carried out. The results revealed markedly elevated
concentrations of petroleum hydrocarbons in soils at refining sites compared with background
locations and applicable regulatory standards, with distinct spatial hotspots occurring in areas
where refining activities persisted for longer durations. PAH profiles showed predominance of
higher-molecular-weight, persistent compounds, including those with known carcinogenicity. Risk
calculations signaled both ecological and human-health concerns. The findings point to the need
for targeted remediation, continuous environmental monitoring, stronger enforcement of
regulations and community-centered alternatives to artisanal refining. The study provides a
baseline for remediation planning and for policymaking to reduce long-term environmental and
public-health burdens in Bayelsa

key: assessing socio economic carrying capacity of tiworo watershed muna island indonesia
title: Assessing Socio-Economic Carrying Capacity of Tiworo Watershed, Muna Island, Indonesia
abstract: Watershed degradation in small islands is increasingly influenced by socio-economic pressures such as population growth, poverty, and weak governance. Therefore, this research aimed to assess the socio-economic carrying capacity of Tiworo Watershed on Muna Island. This research was conducted from March to June 2022 across Muna Regency and West Muna Regency. The analysis used three parameters in accordance with Ministerial Regulation No. P.61/Menhut-II/2014, namely population pressure, population welfare, as well as the existence and enforcement of rules. The researchers collected primary data through purposive sampling from local stakeholders and households, while secondary data originated from Badan Pusat Statistik (BPS) and local agencies. The results showed that the population pressure was 1.39 ha/household, indicating a moderate level. The population welfare level was categorized as poor (29.5% of households), with increasing dependence on forest resources and the potential for land conversion. Rule existence and enforcement were categorized as good because local communities still maintain local norms and practices, including spring protection and agroforestry. The overall socio-economic carrying capacity score was 105, placing the watershed in the moderate category. Strengthening welfare, land-use planning, and local wisdom-based management is necessary to support sustainable watershed governance.

key: the west crimean sevastopol earthquake of june 22 2026
title: The West Crimean (Sevastopol) earthquake of June 22, 2026
abstract: The article studies a series of earthquakes that occurred from June 22 to July 3, 2026, in the southern part of the Crimean Peninsula shelf zone, in the Sevastopol subzone of the Crimean seismogenic zone (CSZ). The results of instrumental data on the strongest earthquake on June 22, 2026 at 05:48 with Mw=4.0 are presented. In this zone, a historical destructive earthquake is known in 1650 with M=7.0, I0=9 points, on December 8, 1793with M=5.5, I0=6 points, on July 25, 1875 with M=5.2, I0=7–8 points, on March 18, 1957 with M=5.5, I0=6–7 points MSK-64. The parameters of the June 22, 2026 earthquakes were determined using instrumental data from seismic stations of the Geophysical Survey of the Russian Academy of Sciences in the Caucasus and the Crimean network. Data from individual European and Turkish stations were also used. A focal mechanism was determined based on the signs of the first arrival of P-waves at 40 seismic stations. A normal fault was established at the source. The spectral parameters of the source of the studied earthquake were calculated: seismic moment M0, rupture radius R and stress drops Δσ. Tectonically, the studied earthquakes of the Sevastopol subzone are located within the Crimean part of the West Crimean Fault, which bounds fold-and-thrust dislocations of the Cenozoic cover within the underwater part of the Crimean Orogen from the west. A ring shaped structure formed by crustal earthquakes with depths h=0–33 km and a threshold magnitude of Mt=3.7 has appeared in the south of Crimea and the adjacent Black Sea. Another ring structure, formed by deep earthquakes (h=34–70 km), is located in the Black Sea, to the east of the shallow structure. The ring seismic structures are in contact near the epicentral zone of the Yalta earthquake of 1927. The magnitude of a possible strong earthquake has been estimated at Mw=6.7±0.4. It is assumed that such an event is likely to occur before 2039.

key: occupation illegale de la baie de ngaliema enjeux ecologiques et risques pour la securite
title: OCCUPATION ILLÉGALE DE LA BAIE DE NGALIEMA : ENJEUX ÉCOLOGIQUES ET RISQUES POUR LA SÉCURITÉ HYDRIQUE DE KINSHASA
abstract:
Ngaliema Bay cannot be viewed simply as a basic land reserve available for urban expansion. It constitutes both a riparian area along the Congo River, an ecological transition zone, and the immediate setting for strategic infrastructure for the abstraction and supply of drinking water. However, the embankments, housing estates and buildings springing up there in breach of legal restrictions are gradually altering the bay’s geography, reducing wetland areas and disrupting the operational conditions of the Ngaliema plant’s water intake. Based on a documentary, legal and diachronic analysis of satellite imagery from 2005 and 2025, this article argues that the illegal occupation of the bay creates a dual vulnerability: ecological, through the alteration of riparian habitats and the environment’s regulatory functions; infrastructural and humanitarian, by exposing an essential public service to obstruction, silting, pollution and difficulties in accessing the infrastructure. The study shows that the problem falls within the remit of neither town planning nor land management; it concerns the water security of Kinshasa and calls for an integrated response combining prevention, preparedness, response, resilience, recovery, reintegration and stabilisation. We propose the concept of urban water sovereignty to describe the state’s capacity to sustainably protect the areas, standards and infrastructure on which collective access to drinking water depends.
Keywords : Ngaliema Bay; environmental issues; illegal occupation; water security.

key: analysis of the minutes of rondas campesinas using text mining techniques
title: Analysis of the minutes of rondas campesinas using text mining techniques
abstract: The rondas campesinas are rural community justice organizations that emerged among impoverished indigenous communities in the Andes and are the driving force behind the largest and most influential grassroots movement in north-eastern Peru. The aim of the research was to unveil the characteristics, thematic approaches and working dynamics of the rondas campesinas using text mining as a technique for information analysis. Seventy-four minutes from Huaquillas, Namballe and San Jose de Lourdes in the province of San Ignacio, department of Cajamarca were analyzed, covering the period from 2012 to 2024. The analysis included five steps: data collection and pre-processing by eliminating stopwords and tokenization, keyword identification using the word cloud technique, word quantification using the Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency method, latent topic analysis through Latent Dirichlet assignment and vector representation through modeling with Word2Vec. These steps allowed the identification of community problems, social control actions and emerging trends in community organization. The text mining technique is a tool to analyze minutes not only of rondas campesinas but also of organizations or institutions that want to know with certainty the thematic approaches they develop.

key: evaluation of environmental control efforts at the kejawanan nusantara fishing port based
title: EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL CONTROL EFFORTS AT THE KEJAWANAN NUSANTARA FISHING PORT BASED ON THE K5 PRINCIPLES
abstract: The increase in economic activity in the Kejawanan Nusantara Fishing Port area has created quite complex environmental problems. To address these problems, the Kejawanan Nusantara Fishing Port has implemented the K5 principles (cleanliness, aesthetics, security, order, and occupational safety). However, the extent of their success remains uncertain. This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of implementing the K5 principles as the basis for environmental control at the Kejawanan Nusantara Fishing Port, Cirebon City. This study used a descriptive quantitative and qualitative evaluative approach through field observations, in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, and the distribution of questionnaires to 75 respondents consisting of port managers, security officers, cleaning officers, government agencies, fishermen, business actors, and marine tourism visitors. The evaluation results showed that the implementation of the K5 principles at Kejawanan Nusantara Fishing Port was in the good category with an average score of 3.82. The highest score was obtained for the cleanliness aspect (4.05) and the lowest for the orderliness aspect (3.55). The success factors in environmental control were supported by the availability of a wastewater treatment plant (WWTP), the involvement of cleaning personnel, and the implementation of occupational safety standards. The main obstacles were limited human resources, weak coordination between agencies, and low awareness of environmentally friendly behavior among port users. Priority strategies for environmental control were identified in the ecological dimension, such as improving WWTP facilities, solid waste management, and port drainage rehabilitation.

key: geography agriculture and structural transformation in south asia a descriptive analysis o
title: Geography, Agriculture, and Structural Transformation in South Asia: A Descriptive Analysis of Agricultural Value Added (% of GDP), 2010–2025
venue: European Journal of Prosthodontics and Restorative Dentistry
abstract: Over the years, agriculture has been the mainstay of economies and rural livelihoods in South Asia, but as countries turn to industry and services, its contribution to gross domestic product has steadily decreased. Using the countries of India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives, and Afghanistan as reference points, the study uses value added in agriculture, forestry and fishing, percentage of GDP from 2010–2025 to show the impact on changes (World Bank, 2025a). The analysis is based solely on open-source data, specifically the NV.AGR.TOTL.ZS indicator from the World Bank, which is compiled from national accounts, statistical offices, and central banks. This analysis indicates that the regional average has hovered around 15.7% in recent years, with higher levels observed a decade earlier, although this has displayed considerable variation (Trading Economics, 2024; World Bank, 2025b). The essence of the paper is that it sorts countries by geography. Rugged highland and landlocked countries like Nepal and Afghanistan still maintain larger shares devoted to agriculture. This is because they grapple with transport problems of being landlocked, and climatic problems of being highland. On the other hand, the large Indo-Gangetic plains in India and Pakistan allow the two countries to diversify faster using irrigation and markets. Furthermore, coastal or island countries such as Bangladesh and Sri Lanka mix in farming with garments tourism or remittances (Asian Development Bank, 2025). Basic tools, namely trend line, average, standard deviation and ranking, reveal patterns that show plains economy shedding agrarian dependence faster than others (Jha & Afrin, 2018). The uneven nature of these paths is reminiscent of old debates on structural transformation whereby it is argued that labour flows from low productivity farms to dynamic sectors to promote growth. However, South Asia’s pace of transformation appears to be far slower than that of East Asia. This has been attributed to traps based on type of terrain combined with a slow pace of industrialisation (Gollin et al. 2014). Policymakers can benefit by boosting agro-processing, rural jobs and resilient value chains to tap the demographic bulge The work aims to prioritize replicable and transparent data. It fills a gap left by recent region-wide snapshots and establishes a baseline for deeper sustainable rural future research.

key: golden opportunities mining production linkages and firm development
title: Golden opportunities: Mining, production linkages, and firm development

key: miners and minors the impact of mineral resource booms on female underage employment
title: Miners and Minors: The Impact of Mineral Resource Booms on Female Underage Employment
abstract: Resource booms are often associated with adverse distributional effects across economies. We exploit temporal and spatial variation generated by the copper boom in the 2000s to measure the effect of mineral resource extraction on human capital investment in Zambia. Combining data from repeated cross-sections of households and mines, we find that adolescent girls near mines have lower school attendance and higher engagement in paid work. We argue that the main pull factor is the increase in the demand for labor among sectors where women typically dominate. As more adult women marry and married women live in households that benefit from the wealth generated by spouses, adolescent girls fill the gap previously met by adult women in the labor market. Our findings suggest that resource booms induce inequitable distributional effects across generations of women.

key: economic environment and social welfare in the mineral economy provinces of eastern indone
title: Economic, Environment, and Social Welfare in the Mineral Economy Provinces of Eastern Indonesia
abstract: This study explores the relationships between economic growth, environmental quality, and social welfare in the mineral economy provinces of Eastern Indonesia, which are heavily dependent on the mining sector—using simultaneous equation models and secondary data from 2015–2022. Empirical results show a bidirectional causal relationship between EQI and HDI, suggesting that improvements in environmental quality enhance human development, and higher human development levels contribute to better environmental quality. Additionally, a unidirectional causal relationship between EQI and GDP indicates that improvements in environmental quality can lead to economic growth. Still, economic growth alone does not necessarily lead to improvements in environmental quality.

key: on the ethical considerations of generative agents
title: On the Ethical Considerations of Generative Agents
abstract: The Generative Agents framework recently developed by Park et al. has enabled numerous new technical solutions and problem-solving approaches. Academic and industrial interest in generative agents has been explosive as a result of the effectiveness of generative agents toward emulating human behaviour. However, it is necessary to consider the ethical challenges and concerns posed by this technique and its usage. In this position paper, we discuss the extant literature that evaluate the ethical considerations regarding generative agents and similar generative tools, and identify additional concerns of significant importance. We also suggest guidelines and necessary future research on how to mitigate some of the ethical issues and systemic risks associated with generative agents.

key: is education neglected in natural resources rich countries an intergenerational approach i
title: Is Education Neglected in Natural Resources-Rich Countries? An Intergenerational Approach in Africa
abstract: The literature on the effects of natural resources on education is mixed and inconclusive. In this paper, we adopt an innovative approach by exploring the effects of mineral discoveries and productions on intergenerational educational mobility (IM), linking parents to the children education levels for more than 14 million individuals across 28 African countries and 2,890 districts. We find that mineral discoveries and productions positively affect educational IM for primary education in Africa for individuals exposed to the mineral sites and living in districts with discoveries. Specifically, the probability of upward primary IM increases by 2.7 percentage points (pp.) following mineral discoveries and 6.7 pp. following mineral productions. Downward primary IM decreases by 1.2 pp. following both mineral discoveries and productions. These positive effects are increasing for individuals born later after discoveries and productions, for males, and individuals living in the urban area. However, no significant effects are found for secondary and tertiary educational IM. Finally, we explore the income and returns to education channels through which mineral discoveries and productions affect educational IM. RECOMMENDED CITATION: Atsebi, J. M. B., Ouedraogo, R. & Seri, R. S. (2022). Is Education Neglected in Natural Resources-Rich Countries? An Intergenerational Approach in Africa, IMF Working Paper, WP/22/160 JEL Classification Numbers: C55; I21; I25; I26; N9; O10; O55; Q32

key: the local economic impact of mineral mining in africa evidence from four decades of satell
title: The Local Economic Impact of Mineral Mining in Africa: Evidence from Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
abstract: Using state-of-the-art techniques in computer vision, we analyze one million satellite images covering 12% of the African continent between 1984 and 2019 to track local development around 1,658 mineral deposits. We use stacked event studies and difference-in-difference models to estimate the impact of mine openings and closings. The magnitude of the effect of mine openings is considerable - after 15 years, urban areas within 20km of an opening mine almost double in size. We find strong evidence of a political resource curse at the local level. Although mining boosts the local economy in democratic countries, these gains are meager in autocracies and come at the expense of tripling the likelihood of conflict relative to prior the onset of mining. Furthermore, our results suggest that the growth acceleration in mining areas is only temporary and diminishes with the closure of the mine.

key: green consumption environmental knowledge environmental consciousness social norms and pur
title: Green consumption: Environmental knowledge, environmental consciousness, social norms, and purchasing behavior
abstract: The 2015 Paris Agreement is the first historical global accord aiming to palliate global warming. Climate change has caused ecological, economic, and social disasters, among other things and has made not only nations review their environmental protection issues but also the consumers paying more attention to the environment and encouraging green oriented buying behaviors. This study targets Taiwan's consumers, and 649 valid questionnaires were recovered. Exploratory factor analysis was applied to extract the trait factors, whereas confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling were used for the verification of the scale and structural model, respectively. The result shows that the consumers' environmental knowledge, environmental consciousness, and the social norms have had a positive effect on their environmental attitude, as do their environmental knowledge and the social norms to a sense of well‐being. Consumers purchasing intention and behavior are pointing towards green products. Therefore, companies need to respond to the consumers' demand and fulfill their social responsibility to release the green products so as to satisfy the consumers' needs.

key: impact of pollution from coal on the anemic status of children and women evidence from ind
title: Impact of Pollution from Coal on the Anemic Status of Children and Women: Evidence from India
abstract: Economic growth in emerging market economies has come hand-in-hand with growing demand for energy, with many of them meeting this higher demand by increased use of coal to fuel electricity generation. This paper examines the impact of pollution generated by coal fueled power units on the anemic status of children and women in India. We show that among very young children (aged 0–5 years), the number of coal units in the district in the month and year of birth significantly increases the likelihood of being anemic net of a comprehensive set of child, mother, household and district level controls. Exposure in utero matters as well for child anemia, while the number of coal plants in the district also induce greater anemia among adult women. Impacts on anemic status are driven by the growth of PM2.5 pollution attributable to emissions from coal-powered units. We undertake a series of falsification and specification checks to underline the robustness of our results. Our research adds anemia to the list of significant health costs of relying on coal-fired power generation in meeting the increasing demand for energy that emerging market economies like India face.

key: evaluation of ambient air particulate matter urine arsenic levels and the effect on reside
title: Evaluation of Ambient Air Particulate Matter, Urine Arsenic Levels and the Effect on Residents Health in an Artisanal Mining Community and an Incorporated Mining Community in Ghana From April 2024 to July 2024: A Cross‐Sectional Study
abstract: Over 200 million people in developing and industrialized countries are exposed to arsenic poisoning. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) constitutes a significant air contaminant, especially in urban and industrial suburbs. A significant proportion of countries do not possess sufficient ambient air quality guidelines for particulate matter pollution, which has the potential for toxicity, including renal toxicity. The health risk of pollution to inhabitants of a mining area is of much concern. The Ghanaian mining sector plays a significant role in the economy, being the largest foreign exchange earner. This study assessed ambient air quality, general health status and biochemical indices of the kidney that might be due to poisoning from mining pollutants such as Arsenic.

key: health at risk investigating the impacts of environmental exposure and water contamination
title: Health at risk: investigating the impacts of environmental exposure and water contamination in emerging economies
abstract: This study analyzes how population health is impacted by environmental degradation, chemical exposure, and water contamination in 35 middle-income countries between 1980 and 2022. To address endogeneity and serial correlation in the panel data, the analysis uses the dynamic ordinary least squares and fully modified ordinary least squares estimators. The empirical findings show a definite trend. Secondary education, access to clean water, improved sanitation facilities, and economic output are positively associated with life expectancy. On the contrary, CO2 emissions, industrial value added, shortage of healthcare resources, and the increased age dependency ratios are negatively correlated with the health outcomes of the population. This result is also true for other specifications and estimation techniques. The main strength of this study is the concurrent analysis of several environmental and socioeconomic factors affecting health in a single empirical model. From a policy perspective, the evidence supports three main directions. Promote cleaner technologies and emission reduction to lessen environmental and health costs, in addition to improvements in access to education and sanitation. Industrial development should be controlled by waste minimization, recycling, and renewable energy.

key: from pollution exposure to health and economic loss microlevel evidence from industrial zo
title: From Pollution Exposure to Health and Economic Loss: Micro‐Level Evidence From Industrial Zones in Bangladesh
abstract:
Rapid industrialization has significantly contributed to economic growth in developing countries, but it has also generated substantial environmental externalities, particularly air pollution. This study investigates the micro‐level relationship between pollution exposure, health outcomes, and household economic burden among communities living near industrial zones in Bangladesh. Using primary survey data from 520 respondents located near the Chattogram Export Processing Zone (EPZ), the analysis constructs a pollution exposure index based on proximity to industrial activity, visible emissions, outdoor exposure, and household ventilation conditions. Health impacts are measured using a composite morbidity index capturing both self‐reported symptoms and medically diagnosed conditions. The study employs Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) to estimate the relationship between pollution exposure and morbidity, and a Generalized Linear Model (GLM) with a Gamma distribution and log link to analyze healthcare expenditure. The results show that higher pollution exposure is significantly associated with higher morbidity levels, even after controlling for socioeconomic and demographic factors. Moreover, increased exposure is associated with higher household healthcare expenditure, with morbidity acting as a key transmission channel. A one‐unit increase in pollution exposure is associated with an approximate 20–25 percent increase in expected medical spending. These findings highlight how industrial pollution imposes significant health and economic burdens on respondents residing near industrial zones and underscore the need for stronger environmental regulation, cleaner industrial technologies, and improved public health interventions to mitigate pollution‐related risks.
